name: cross-corpus-floor
purpose: Doc-15 clean-FLOOR corpus for the end-to-end cross-corpus composition test (nmemo-uhp.19). 40 CLEAR MISRA C++:2023 Chapter-22 violations (4 per rule, varied patterns) + 10 controls (5 out-of-chapter, 5 compliant-Ch.22). Ground truth is by construction. Snippets are illustrative (not compiled), mirroring e2e-misra/queries.json.

caveats.floor: CLEAN floor: clear, surface-observable violations. NOT field prevalence (~44% violations here by construction). NOT implicit-behaviour (OQ1 is a separate tranche). Magnitudes do not transfer.
caveats.rule_text: Rule text = my blind topic restatements, NOT authoritative MISRA C++:2023 text (copyright).
caveats.overlap: Rules 22.1-22.4 (allocation/ownership) inherently overlap; 22.7/22.8 (delete-match/array-delete) and 22.9/22.5 (double-free/dangling) co-occur by construction. Where a snippet genuinely trips >1 rule, ALL are cited (primary_rule marks the intended target). Rule 22.4 (ownership-explicit) is the most semantic/debatable; flagged per element.
caveats.ground_truth: expected_rule_citations authored by me; the pre-committed adversary (doc 15 §6) audits them.

rules.text: Dynamic heap allocation shall not be used in safety-critical or hard real-time code paths.
Dynamically allocated resources shall be managed using RAII so acquisition and release are tied to object lifetime.
Dynamically allocated memory shall be owned through smart pointers rather than raw owning pointers.
Ownership of a dynamically allocated resource shall be explicit and unambiguous.
A pointer shall not be dereferenced after the object it refers to has ended its lifetime (no dangling pointer dereference).
Arithmetic on raw pointers shall not be performed; bounded abstractions shall be used instead.
A resource released with delete shall have been allocated with the matching new form.
Memory allocated with array new[] shall be released with array delete[].
A dynamically allocated resource shall not be released more than once (no double free).
A weak pointer shall be locked to obtain a valid owning pointer, and null-checked, before use.
